messages:
maria gonzalez: Heads-up — PR #7033 (adaptive-batcher) landed in canary last night. Nightly perf run shows a tail latency bump on mixed long-seq workloads (12-18% p95/p99). linking results: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/7033

oliver chan: ugh. thanks for the ping. do we have the bench output? can you paste the relevant numbers?

maria gonzalez: pasted excerpt below. i also attached the full gist but will paste key bits here.
```
workload: mixed-longseq-32k
commit: 7033-adaptive-batcher
metric   main       pr-7033   delta
mean(ms) 45.2       46.0      +1.8%
p95(ms)  88.4       99.0      +12.0%
p99(ms)  120.1      141.8     +18.1%
mem(MB)  1623       1638      +0.9%
throughput(tok/s)  191k  188k   -1.6%
```

kevin li: thanks. that p99 jump is concerning. any logs showing queueing or KV-cache hot paths?

maria gonzalez: i checked traces from canary — increased scheduling wait time on the batcher worker. trace snippet: `batch_wait_ms` went from ~6ms to ~18ms for long sequences. no obvious OOMs.

tara: is the change to prefer latency-friendly microbatches vs throughput batches? PR description said "adaptive batching windows" — maybe heuristic favors coalescing more for short requests but inadvertently stretches long ones.

oliver chan: cc @kevin li — can you run the microbench that isolates batch scheduling (single-worker, mix ratio 70/30 short/long) and attach flame? if it's scheduler, should be visible. i can roll back the canary if needed.

kevin li: starting bench now. will take ~30m. if it's scheduler we can probably tweak the policy to enforce max wait for long-seq requests.

bench-bot: nightly-bench: mixed-longseq-32k on pr-7033 completed. artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/nightly/1989991234/pr-7033-results.json

maria gonzalez: thanks @bench-bot. note: customer test harness also showed a small uptick in request timeouts (non-fatal) during spike window.

oliver chan: if kevin confirms scheduler regression, we should either: 1) hotfix to clamp wait-time by request-length, or 2) revert PR until we land a more selective heuristic. prefer 1 if small change.

kevin li: bench done. flipped on verbose scheduler tracing. quick findings: the adaptive window merged up to 3x more short requests into batches when long requests were present, causing head-of-queue long requests to wait for short-request aggregation. attaching flame link: https://perf.internal/flame/1989991234

tara: ok that matches suspicion. can we add a simple rule: if request.seq_len > threshold => force max_wait_ms = 8? that should bound tail.

maria gonzalez: i can open a follow-up PR with clamp + unit test and bench again. will also add a canary config to disable adaptive merging for canary until we validate.

oliver chan: sounds good. timeline? if you can get PR by EOD we'll re-run canary tonight and decide on revert tomorrow morning.

maria gonzalez: i'll aim for a PR by 1700 PT. tagging reviewers: @oliver chan, @kevin li, @tara.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: rollout paused for service=runtime-canary due to perf-alert at 1989991237. action_required: manual review.

kevin li: thanks for the quick investigation. let me know if you want me to push the clamp patch and run microbench. i can also try a synthetic stress with 10x long seq load.

maria gonzalez: appreciate it. i'll draft the clamp PR and post bench outputs here. if we see <3% tail change it's good to proceed; otherwise we'll revert. :thumbsup:
